FRENCH — TERMLY EXAM #14
====

GRADE: Grade 9
SUBJECT: FRENCH
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. “Bonjour” is used to say: (1 mark)
   A. Good night only
   B. Excuse me
   C. Good morning / hello
   D. Thank you

2. When practising Listening for information Vocabulary Grammar Attention, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Listening for information Vocabulary Grammar Attention.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for information Vocabulary Grammar Attention.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Listening for information Vocabulary Grammar Attention.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for information Vocabulary Grammar Attention.

3. When practising Listening for information, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Listening for information.

   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for information.

   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive speaking.

6. When practising Active Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Active Listening.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Active Listening.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Active Listening.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Active Listening.

7. When practising Oral expression, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Oral expression.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Oral expression.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Oral expression.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Oral expression.

8. When practising Interactive listening 1.3 Active listening 1.4 Listening for information, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Interactive listening 1.3 Active listening 1.4 Listening for information.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive listening 1.3 Active listening 1.4 Listening for information.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Interactive listening 1.3 Active listening 1.4 Listening for information.

9. The French word for “book” is: (1 mark)
   A. porte
   B. chaise
   C. livre
   D. fenêtre

10. When practising Interactive Speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Interactive Speaking.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive Speaking.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Interactive Speaking.

----
